bull_bear.body:
- Part of the Tata Motors ecosystem since 1980 (jointly promoted by Tata Motors and EDC Ltd.), aligning ACGL with Group-wide transformation in electrification, sustainability, safety and digitalisation
- In-house design team, skilled manpower and strong vendor base supporting consistent growth and quality
- Bus segment dominance - 92% of FY26 revenue - with highest-ever annual bus sales of 9,328 units and the milestone rollout of the 100,000th bus, reflecting manufacturing legacy and customer trust
- IATF 16949 quality certification across all three plants
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- ICE-to-EV migration capability constraints — Company flags risk related to capability constraints with respect to the migration of ICE to EV bus bodies, evolving sustainability requirements, and capacity constraints to meet peak and future demand effectively.
- Digital transformation and infrastructure modernization delays — Delays in digital transformation and infrastructure modernization could impact productivity, competitiveness, and progress toward environmental commitments.
- Rising competitive intensity in the electric bus segment — Growing presence of multinational players in the electric vehicle space, coupled with increasing collaborations between local bus body builders and foreign partners, poses competitive pressure on domestic OEMs particularly in the rapidly emerging electric bus segment.
- Geopolitical exposure on exports and input costs — The prevailing geopolitical environment may impact bus exports to the Middle East and lead to an increase in commodity prices; of the 9,328 buses sold in FY26, 3,382 units were exported, indicating meaningful export exposure.
- Single-segment revenue concentration in Bus — The Bus segment's revenue share clocked 92% of total company revenue during the year, making performance highly dependent on demand and pricing in that single segment.
- Cyclicality and OEM-dependence in the Pressing segment — The sheet-metal Pressing business follows the cyclicity of OEM business for which the Company is a key supplier; the segment is capital intensive and capacity utilization drives its profitability, exposing it to swings in OEM order volumes.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: ACGL manufactures all types of bus variants - LCV, ICV, MCV, HCV, sleeper coaches, mobile vans, ambulances and defense vehicles - through an in-house design team, own manufacturing facilities and a strong vendor base. It also runs a capital-intensive sheet-metal Pressing segment that supplies OEMs and follows their business cyclicality. During the year the Company raised its installed manufacturing capacity to 1,200 buses per month, with a higher share of bus bodies built on the MCV platform for State Transport Undertakings (STUs).

- In-house design team, skilled manpower and strong vendor base supporting consistent growth and quality
- Bus segment dominance - 92% of FY26 revenue - with highest-ever annual bus sales of 9,328 units and the milestone rollout of the 100,000th bus, reflecting manufacturing legacy and customer trust
- IATF 16949 quality certification across all three plants
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Building a future-ready and sustainable mobility solutions organisation, anchored in operational excellence, innovation, sustainability and customer trust
- Strengthening engineering, manufacturing and digital capabilities to support next-generation mobility solutions, including emerging electric vehicle applications
- Sustainability integral to long-term strategy - renewable energy adoption, water conservation, waste management and greenhouse-gas/carbon-footprint reduction, aligned with Tata Group sustainability commitments
- Strengthening operational excellence framework through process automation, digital integration and enhanced monitoring systems across functions
- Entry into electric bus body manufacturing and focus on higher-tonnage buses to enhance price realisation per bus body
- Product diversification - expanding into school, staff and electric vehicle (EV) segments with new, contemporary designs to broaden the product range
- Cost reduction initiatives to mitigate potential adverse effects of the geopolitical situation on commodity prices
- Technology absorption focus - PLM implementation, ABS dashboard development for Middle East markets, defence and EV vehicle development
- This bundle does not include a stated broader capital-allocation or dividend-policy philosophy; it only records that the Notice of the 46th AGM seeks shareholder approval to declare a Final Dividend of Rs. 22.50 per equity share of face value Rs.10 each (225%) for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2025-26 ACGL's capex activity was concentrated on sustainability and digital infrastructure rather than a single named capacity project: a 500 kWp solar power plant was commissioned at the Goa facility and an 805 kWp rooftop solar installation was commissioned at the Jejuri plant; new Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) of 50 KLD and 80 KLD capacity were commissioned at the Goa facilities along with supporting pipeline infrastructure; a rainwater harvesting lake of approximately 85 lakh litres storage capacity, with six groundwater recharge wells, is under development at Goa; and food waste composting facilities with cumulative processing capacity of 550 kg/day were commissioned at the Goa plants. On the digital side, the Company initiated an ERP migration to SAP's latest technology roadmap for a scalable, future-ready ERP environment, launched a Cybersecurity Enhancement programme, and digitized its procurement approval and RFQ processes. Separately, at its Business Partners Meet 2026 (6 March 2026, Bhuimpal, Goa) the Company outlined future growth plans that include scaling supplier capacity to support production and delivery of 12,000 buses per annum.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Commercial vehicle segment, especially buses, poised for positive growth driven by increased government investment in public transportation and electrification initiatives
- Growth supported by enabling policies - the Vehicle Scrappage Policy, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, infrastructure development to reduce logistics costs, and EV-focused measures like FAME and the Payment Security Guarantee
- Bus segment momentum driven by demand from State Transport Undertakings (STUs), institutional transportation, employee mobility and increasing focus on sustainable public transportation
- Rationalisation of GST rates between fully built vehicles and separately supplied bus bodies expected to support growth of OEM-supplied bus bodies
- Government focus on infrastructure development, including highways, to promote electric mobility seen as an opportunity for growth in commercial vehicles and mass transportation solutions
- Threat from growing presence of multinational players in the EV space and increasing collaborations between local bus body builders and foreign partners, creating competitive pressure in the emerging electric bus segment
- Geopolitical environment (developments in the Middle East) may impact bus exports and lead to an increase in commodity prices
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: ACGL, jointly promoted in 1980 by Tata Motors Ltd. and EDC Ltd., was the first major engineering unit set up in Goa and is today a leading manufacturer of bus bodies across all vehicle categories, part of the Tata Motors ecosystem.

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 22.50 per equity share (225%) for FY2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
Company is making efforts to penetrate bus body manufacturing of electric buses, viewed as the future technology in passenger mobility.
Company is focusing on higher tonnage buses to enhance price realisation per bus body.
Company is undertaking a phased infrastructure upgrade aligned with projected future demand, with strategic investments planned in digitisation, sustainability and EV manufacturing capabilities.
Development of TATA Lake, an artificial water body with 85 lakh litres storage capacity at Goa, was initiated to help achieve zero liquid discharge (ZLD) and support groundwater recharge.
Company is accelerating implementation of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems in product design and expanding digitisation across HR and operations.
Company may face risks related to capability constraints in migrating from ICE to EV bus bodies, evolving sustainability requirements, and capacity constraints in meeting peak and future demand.
Delays in digital transformation and infrastructure modernization could impact productivity, competitiveness and progress toward environmental commitments.
Prevailing geopolitical environment may impact bus exports to the Middle East and lead to an increase in commodity prices.
Strategic investments in digitisation, sustainability and EV manufacturing capabilities aim to advance long-term objectives including the transition towards net-zero emissions.
Development of a 13.5 m EV Sleeper bus has been initiated.
As part of future growth plans outlined at the Business Partners Meet 2026, ACGL is scaling supplier capacity to support production and delivery of 12,000 buses per annum.
A rainwater harvesting lake of approximately 85 lakh litres storage capacity, including six groundwater recharge wells, is under development at Goa.
Company initiated migration to SAP's latest technology roadmap for business process integration, improved reporting and real-time analytics, providing a scalable future-ready ERP environment.
Company initiated a comprehensive Cybersecurity Enhancement programme covering security assessments, vulnerability remediation, access controls and continuous monitoring.
